# jochwacht-sbom 0.21.0 — sends the full bill, ships with its own SBOM

**`--send` uploads the full bill.** Up to 0.20.0 the upload carried names,
versions and your own declarations only. From 0.21.0 it is the local bill
with every field it holds: every component with name, version and purl, and
licence, CPE and manufacturer where your build or lockfile states them; and
from a Yocto or Buildroot build directory the delivered files (their names
or paths inside the image, with SHA-512), the image files, patches by type
and the creator the build proves. It is written first to `.jochwacht/sent.cdx.json`, exactly as sent,
and the summary before sending says what goes up. Two things never go up:

- the text of a patch: the upload names each patch by its SHA-256 and size
  (it can be your own source code; TR-03183 does not ask for it);
- the name of the scanned folder: the product name is the one your build
  states, else `--product`, else `product`.

No absolute path, host name or user name is in it.

- **When an upload is `unchanged`.** The README now says how the server
  decides: only the components (name, version, purl, CPE) make a new
  version. A new build with the same components but other bytes is a new
  file state of the current version: no new run, no report, no alarm, and it
  does not count against the daily limit (details in the README).
- **The binary has its own SBOM.** Each release now carries
  `jochwacht-sbom-<version>-linux-x86_64.cdx.json` with its `.sha256` beside
  the binary: Python and every bundled library, from PyInstaller's table of
  contents and the locked build environment.
- **Release gate.** Nothing is published while a library of the wheel's
  locked resolution or of the binary has a known vulnerability: pip-audit
  checks the hashed lock files in `ci/release/` before the PyPI and the
  binary upload, with no exception list. The binary is built from exactly
  those locks. pip on your machine resolves the wheel's dependencies anew.
- Every GitHub Action of the release is pinned to a full commit SHA.
- The binary no longer bundles setuptools, which it never used.
- A patch type in Buildroot's SBOM that is no string (for example
  `"type": []`) is no valid type. In 0.20.0 it made every Buildroot package
  drop out with exit 1. Buildroot's SBOM as JSON without an object at its
  root is now named; 0.20.0 skipped it without a word.
- The seven old `sbom.cdx*.json` files are gone from the repository root.
